chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Usama; and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Usama and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Is'haq — from one whom he trusts among the companions of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) — that
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, indeed You do not leave Your earth empty of a Divine Authority of Yours over Your creatures.'

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: Allahumma — a vocative form of address to God used in supplication
key_terms.حُجَّة: Hujja (Divine Proof/Authority) — the Imam or Prophet appointed by God as proof upon creation
key_terms.خَلْق: Khalq (creation/creatures) — all of creation, particularly human beings who bear moral responsibility

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the earth never being empty of a Divine Authority?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) supplicated affirming that Allah never leaves the earth without a Proof (Hujja) — a Divine Authority to guide humanity. This theological affirmation, transmitted through a chain of trusted companions, establishes the Shia doctrine that the earth always has an Imam or Divine Authority, whether manifest or in occultation. The audience of early Shia Muslims would have understood 'Hujja' as a technical term for the infallible Imam appointed by God.
